definition: Self-evaluation is the process of judging oneself, including one’s worth and how one compares with others. In this context, it is a key pathway through which social media feedback can affect psychological distress.

reasons: The packet supports self-evaluation as a mechanism/pathway linking social media feedback to psychological distress, but it does not define self-evaluation as judging one’s worth or comparing oneself with others.
The comparison-with-others and worth language is not stated in the source; it looks like an unsupported conflation with self-esteem and social comparison.

The definition states that self-evaluation involves “judging oneself, including one’s worth and how one compares with others,” but the packet only refers to “self-evaluation mechanisms” without defining self-evaluation in those terms.

The claim that, in this context, it is “a key pathway through which social media feedback can affect psychological distress” is directionally supported by the packet (“primarily through self-evaluation mechanisms”), but the definition’s broader characterization of self-evaluation is not supported by the packet.
